subject: Security discovery: snapshot vs backup retention & deletion clarifications
messages:

Cc: security_ops@medinnovate.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from call – vendor SQ + retention clarifications

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier today — good overview of Redwood's serving architecture. Security ops and I had a couple of follow-ups specific to log retention and backups before we start the vendor questionnaire. Attaching the baseline vendor security questionnaire for context.

Top questions we want clarified up front:
- Snapshot vs backup retention: are snapshots considered part of the same retention window as backups? If a customer requests deletion, what is the timeline for removing data from snapshots?
- Restore window / RTO expectations for snapshot restores and whether those restores are retained beyond the backup TTL.
- Is irrecoverable deletion (from backups) performed within an SLA (e.g., X days after request)? Do you have a documented retention matrix?
- Encryption lifecycle for backups (KMS rotation, who holds keys for private deployments).
- Any SOC 2 evidence around backup testing and restore exercises.

Can you send a short matrix or point us to a doc that maps: data class -> snapshot TTL -> backup TTL -> deletion flow? Also, please let us know Redwood's current SOC 2 status and HIPAA alignment notes so we can include them with procurement.

Attached: MedInnovate_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (section A is our initial pass)

Appreciate a short reply and proposed next steps — if helpful we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with our security engineer.

Thanks,
Emma Ruiz
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedInnovate Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list, and great to meet you on the call. Looping Ben (security & compliance) and Marissa (solutions) so they can chime in with specifics.

High-level answers and next steps below; I attached a compact retention matrix (redwood-log-retention-matrix.xlsx) to make this easier to scan.

Quick answers:
- Snapshots vs backups: by default we treat snapshots as point-in-time copies that are stored on the same logical retention schedule as backups for the purposes of deletion requests. Snapshots created for short-term internal operations (e.g., upgrades) can be tagged as ephemeral and have a shorter TTL.
- Deletion SLA: for hosted customers we commit to removing production data from the active storage tier within 48 hours of a verified request; propagation into immutable backup storage and final irreversible deletion follows our backup TTL and certified purge procedure (typical irreversible deletion window: up to 90 days unless a shorter retention is requested and contractually agreed).
- Restore window / RTO: standard RTO for snapshot restores is <4 hours for the model inference clusters we host; for large dataset restores or cross-region restores it can be longer — we document expected RTO per plan in the SLA.
- Encryption & key management: hosted: we manage KMS; keys rotated per our policy (90 days rotation cadence). Private/VPC: customers can provide KMS/HSM keys and control rotation.
- SOC 2 / HIPAA: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in production (report available under NDA); we also provide a HIPAA-ready deployment pattern and BAAs for eligible contracts. Ben will attach the SOC 2 evidence checklist we typically share with procurement.

Action items:
1) Ben to add technical detail around backup immutability, snapshot tagging, and the irreversible deletion flow.
2) Marissa to supply the procurement-friendly summary and the NDA link for SOC 2 report access.
3) Karthik -> propose 30-min deep-dive with your security engineer; I have availability Wed 21 Jan 10–11 PT or Thu 22 Jan 14–15 PT.

If there's anything urgent we missed, flag it here and we can adjust.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Emma — adding a few technical clarifications and the usual security Ops points we include in questionnaires. Quoting Karthik below for context.

Key technical notes:
- Default backup TTL: 90 days for hosted; customers can contract shorter or longer retention. Backups are incremental-forever with periodic full snapshots for efficient restores.
- Snapshot tagging: snapshots have metadata flags (purpose: user-initiated / system-upgrade / analytical) — deletion semantics respect tags. User-initiated data deletions trigger a cascade: mark objects deleted -> remove from active index -> flagged for backup purge. Purge job runs daily; final irrevocable purge from cold backup copies occurs per the configured TTL and requires integrity checks.
- Soft-delete vs permanent erase: soft-delete is immediate (object marked as deleted and hidden from read queries). Permanent erase (cryptographic wipe / removal from backups) follows company's purge SLA; for hosted customers we aim for final removal within 90 days unless legal hold applies.
- Backups & immutable storage: our backup pipeline writes to an immutable append-only store; backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and keys are stored in KMS. For Private deployments, we recommend customer-managed KMS to satisfy stricter compliance needs.
- Evidence & testing: we run quarterly restore drills and record outcomes; the SOC 2 report includes summaries of backup testing frequency and findings.

Open question for MedInnovate: are there legal e-discovery or regulatory hold policies that would require us to delay purge beyond the standard TTL? If yes, please flag the relevant legal team contact so we can include an exception in the contract.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

2) For the 90-day irreversible deletion window: can you confirm whether that 90 days can be shortened by contract for our account (MedInnovate) and, if so, whether there is a cost / operational impact?
